dataset_info.name: VEDA AyurMind AI — Diseases & Therapeutic Herbs Dataset
dataset_info.part_description: Diseases DIS-121 to DIS-145 (H to W) + Complete Sanskrit Terms Master Index
dataset_info.source_text: Dravyaguna Vijnana — Therapeutic Indication of Drugs & Technical Medical Terminology
dataset_info.description: Part 3 of 3 — Final diseases (DIS-121 to DIS-145) covering H to W, plus the complete master index of all 178 Sanskrit technical terms from Part 2 of the source text.
dataset_info.note_on_count: Total unique clinical disease entries = 145. Original Step-1 extraction counted 190 raw text entries because sub-diseases, procedural categories and minor variants were listed separately. In this dataset, entries with fewer than 2 herbs and no unique Sanskrit terms are merged into their parent disease for a cleaner, production-quality database.

diseases.description: Pain in the head or upper neck. Classified as Vataja (throbbing, variable), Pittaja (burning, temporal), Kaphaja (dull, heavy) and Suryavarta (sun-rise headache that worsens with the sun and subsides at sunset).

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: A type of headache beginning with sunrise, increasing with the sun's movement and subsiding at sunset

diseases.description: Involuntary passage of urine; inability to control urinary flow. May be stress, urge or overflow type. Related to weakened Apana Vata in Ayurveda.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Dysuria associated with burning sensation, yellow urine or haematuria

diseases.description: Obstruction or suppression of normal urine flow; anuria or oliguria from obstruction, dehydration or renal compromise.
Obstruction or difficulty during childbirth from abnormal foetal presentation, uterine inertia or birth canal narrowing. Requires obstetric intervention.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Difficult and delayed labour; abnormal posture of foetus

diseases.description: Substances or procedures to accelerate or facilitate delivery when labour is delayed or prolonged.
Retained placenta after delivery; failure of complete placental expulsion causing haemorrhage and infection risk. Requires urgent treatment.
Treatment to prevent miscarriage and promote healthy foetal development and implantation. Part of Garbhini Paricharya (antenatal care) in Ayurveda.
Wasting condition associated with chest injury, pulmonary damage or deep thoracic wounds; presents with chronic cough, haemoptysis, weight loss and progressive debility.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Wasting condition of body due to chest-wound

diseases.description: Painful purulent infection around a fingernail or toenail (paronychia); may involve the nail plate (onychia). Caused by bacterial or fungal infection of the nail fold.

Break in continuity of skin or tissue due to injury; requires cleaning, healing and protection from infection. Ayurveda classifies Vrana as Nija (endogenous) and Agantuja (traumatic); 60 types described in Sushruta Samhita.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Purification; radical elimination of morbid substances

diseases.description: Inflammatory enlargement of cervical lymph nodes forming a chain-like swelling in the neck. May be bacterial, tuberculous or reactive. Distinguished from Apaci (scrofula) by extent and acuity.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Cervical adenitis; chain of swollen glands in neck
Glandular enlargement, swelling and other symptoms

diseases.description: Herbs used for skin care, complexion improvement, beauty enhancement and skin brightening. Varnya herbs improve skin colour; Tvacya herbs protect and nourish skin. Important in Ayurvedic cosmetology (Saundarya Chikitsa).

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Useful in promoting complexion of the skin (pigmentation)
Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Small rough growth on skin caused by HPV (human papillomavirus) infection; benign but contagious.
Excessive sleepiness or abnormal drowsiness during waking hours; reduced alertness. Caused by Kapha and Tamas predominance in Ayurveda.
Abnormal or unpleasant body odour from sweat, skin or breath; may relate to metabolic, digestive or dermatological pathology and Ama accumulation.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Purification; radical elimination of morbid substances

diseases.description: Therapeutic use of medicated smoke (Dhupana) for purification of environment, treatment of skin conditions, respiratory disorders and protection against infectious agents.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Purification; radical elimination of morbid substances

diseases.description: Substances that induce vomiting for therapeutic Panchakarma purification (Vamana karma); one of the five classical Panchakarma procedures used to eliminate excess Kapha.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Emetic; aid to emetics or emesis
Purification; radical elimination of morbid substances

diseases.description: Substances inducing therapeutic purgation (Virechana karma) for elimination of excess Pitta and Pitta-associated toxins; one of the five Panchakarma procedures.
Substances used to remove unwanted hair from the body. Referenced in classical Ayurvedic texts for cosmetic and therapeutic applications.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Sensation of spinning, loss of balance, dizziness or spatial disorientation. Caused by Pitta vitiation in Ayurveda; may involve inner ear, neurological or cardiovascular causes.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Giddiness; mental confusion and delusion; vertigo

diseases.description: State of stupor, confusion or reduced consciousness due to toxic substances, narcotics or severe metabolic derangement.
Pathological conditions affecting semen quality, quantity, viscosity or composition; includes oligospermia, azoospermia and abnormal seminal discharge.
Multiple erupting boils or vesicular skin eruptions; cluster of raised pus-filled lesions. Associated with Pitta and Rakta vitiation causing skin eruptions.
Painful fissures and cracks in the skin of the heels and soles; caused by dry skin, Vata aggravation, nutritional deficiency or pressure on the feet.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: General category of mental and psychiatric disorders. Includes Manasika Rogas (psychic diseases) caused by Raja and Tamas imbalance in the mind (Manas). Encompasses depression, anxiety, psychosis and cognitive disorders.

sanskrit_terms_master_index.description: Complete master index of all 178 Sanskrit technical terms extracted from Part 2 (pages 18-32) of Dravyaguna Vijnana. Includes disease names, pharmacological actions, tissue effects and Ayurvedic principles.
